title: Personal Checking: electronic dispute notice window and provisional credit deadlines by tier
content:
## Scope

This card lists the three time figures that govern an electronic-transaction dispute on a Personal Checking account: the notice window counted from the disputed item's posted date, the standard provisional credit deadline counted from the notice date, and the longer deadline used for a recently opened account.

## Figures by tier

| Tier | Notice window: calendar days after the disputed item's posted date | Provisional credit deadline: business days after the notice date | Deadline used instead for a recently opened account: business days after the notice date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Student Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Everyday Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Interest Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Premier Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |
| Private Client Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 |

- **Notice window**: calendar days after the disputed item's posted date within which a notice qualifies for the electronic dispute process.
- **Provisional credit deadline**: business days after the notice date by which a provisional credit is owed on an open electronic-transaction dispute.
- **Recently opened account deadline**: the provisional credit deadline used instead when the account was opened fewer than the new-account period's calendar days before the notice date.

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Do the dispute figures change with the tier?**
A: No. All six tiers use 120 calendar days, 10 business days and 20 business days.

**Q: Which deadline is counted in calendar days and which in business days?**
A: The notice window is counted in calendar days; both provisional credit deadlines are counted in business days.

**Q: When does the 20-business-day figure replace the 10-business-day figure?**
A: Only when the account was opened fewer than the new-account period's calendar days before the notice date.
